The Alexander Jannaeus page has no Edom, Idumea, Negev or Beersheba holding, only Moab and Galaaditis, 'later returned'. The Hauran part was harmful: 'northern Hauran' was Hauran minus the Cliopatria Nabataean -64 shape, a 40 km Bosra disc and Gilead. The -64 shape covers the Lajat (Trachonitis) and the Nuqrah (Batanaea) up to 33.3 N, and the Bosra disc reaches about 32.88 N (Suwayda, Shahba). The Hauran page: 'the Romans transferred the districts to their Judean client king, Herod the Great in 23 BC'; 'Herod ... establishing permanent colonies and a network of forts in the less vulnerable Batanea district'; the boundary 'just north of the Adraa-Bosra-Salkhad line that had separated the Herodian and Nabatean kingdoms'.
